title: Common-area and lift/lobby service schedules
audience: Cleaners and supervisors who service common areas, lifts and lobbies on a schedule.
learningOutcomes: Build a service schedule for common areas, lifts and lobbies that shows frequency and method.
Keep lift cars and lift controls clean without working on the lift mechanism.
Schedule work around peak use and keep a record of each visit.

instruction.heading: Building the schedule
instruction.body:
A common-area schedule is the agreement between the cleaner and the building manager about what is cleaned, how often, how, with which products and in what time window. Start by walking the building with the manager and listing each area: the lobby floor and entrance mats, the lift cars, the lift lobbies, the stairwells, the corridors, the letterboxes, the bin areas, the glass doors and the handrails. For each area, record the frequency, the method, the products, the equipment and the time window. Frequencies are a matter for the building manager and the strata committee's arrangements. Any frequency written in a training example is an example only.

High-touch points are the surfaces that many people touch in a day, such as lift buttons, handrails, door plates, intercom panels and letterbox handles. They are usually cleaned more often than corridors or stairwells. Set those surfaces out on their own line in the schedule, so that a visit cannot skip them because the rest of the area looked clean. Record the agreed frequency in writing, and keep the copy on site. Do not work from memory, because a schedule that lives in one person's head cannot be checked or handed over.

Build in a review point. A schedule that is set once and never revisited can drift from what the building needs, especially after a change in use, a new tenant mix or a new fitout. Record the date of the last review and the person who agreed the change.

instruction.heading: Lift cars and controls
instruction.body: Clean lift car walls, floors, handrails, mirrors and the outside faces of the call buttons and panels with approved methods. Keep liquid away from the buttons, the display and any gap in the panel, because liquid can get into the controls. Apply product to the cloth first, then wipe the surface, rather than spraying the panel directly. Dry the surface afterwards so that no film builds up on the buttons or the floor. Do not open the lift panels, the machine room or the shaft, and do not work on the lift mechanism, the doors or the sensors. Those parts are maintenance and repair work for the lift service company. The New South Wales WorkSafe guidance on lifts states that the people who have management or control of a lift must make sure it is inspected and maintained regularly, and that records of inspection and maintenance must be kept (SafeWork NSW, lifts and escalators page; modified 28 July 2023). In Queensland, the licence categories on the WorkSafe Queensland lifts page name installation of a new unit and repair or modernisation of an existing unit as licensed work, and the page does not mention servicing or cleaning (WorkSafe Queensland, lifts and escalators licence page; no date shown). Report faults at once, such as a sticking button, a sensor that does not respond, a light that is out or a door that does not close fully. The NSW guidance says that when a lift malfunctions, the lift service company should be called to help anyone trapped, and that the service company or building management must take the lift out of service until it is repaired (SafeWork NSW, lifts and escalators page; modified 28 July 2023). Your role is to stop use where the manager agrees, put up a notice, and report it. It is not to try the repair.

instruction.heading: Peak use, closures and the visit record
instruction.body:
Schedule the heavier work outside peak use, such as the early morning or late evening in a residential block, or the quieter part of the day in a commercial building. Put up signs and barriers where the lobby is in use, and keep walkways clear. Where a lift or a lobby must close for cleaning, agree the closure time with the manager, and give notice to the people who use it in the way the manager has agreed.

Keep a visit record for each area. Record the date, the time, the method, the products, any defect found and the name of the person who did the work. A missed visit is recorded as missed, with the reason, and the manager is told at once. A blank line in a visit record looks the same as a visit that was not done, so the record must show the difference. A complete record is the main evidence that the schedule was met.

procedure: Walk the building with the manager and list each common area, lift and lobby.
Build the schedule with the manager: area, frequency, method, products, equipment and time window, with high-touch points on their own lines.
Clean lift surfaces with approved methods, keeping liquid away from buttons and panels, and dry the surface afterwards.
Do not open lift panels, the machine room or the shaft, and do not work on the mechanism, doors or sensors.
Report lift and door faults at once, and stop use where the manager agrees, with a notice in place.
Schedule heavy work outside peak use, put up signs and barriers, and agree any closure and notice with the manager.
Record each visit with the time, method, products, defects and the person who did the work, and record any missed visit as missed with the reason.

workedExamples.situation: A lift button sticks during the lobby clean, and the car door takes longer than usual to close.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not open the panel or try to fix the button, and do not work on the door. Tell the manager at once. If the manager agrees, take the lift out of use, put up a notice, and call the lift service company as the building's arrangements require. Record the time, the fault and who was told. Do not carry on cleaning inside the car until the fault has been dealt with.

workedExamples.situation: A spill of cleaning liquid runs down the inside of a lift car towards the control panel. A resident is waiting in the lobby for the lift.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do you clean the car, and what do you tell the manager?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop applying liquid to the car. Wipe the spill away from the panel with a dry or lightly damp cloth, keeping liquid off the buttons and display. Dry the floor and mark it as wet. Check the panel from the outside, and report any button that does not respond to the manager. Record the spill, the time and the product used, and ask the manager whether the lift should be out of use while the panel is checked by the service company.

workedExamples.situation: For example, the building's peak use is between 7 am and 9 am on weekdays, and the lobby floor needs a full wet clean that takes about an hour (example times only).
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: When is the work scheduled, and what is put in place?
workedExamples.reasoning: Schedule the wet clean outside the peak window, for example mid-morning, and agree that time with the manager. Put up signs and barriers at the entrance, keep a clear walkway for residents, and record the agreed window in the schedule. Record the visit with the time, the method and the products used.

equipmentAndPpe: Schedule template and visit record, kept on site.
Approved lift and lobby products, each with its label and SDS on hand.
Microfibre cloths for the lift car and controls, and separate cloths for the floor.
Signs, barriers and wet-floor warning signs.
Gloves and eye protection as the SDS requires.
Notice template for closures, agreed with the manager.

commonErrors.error: Spraying liquid directly into a lift panel or onto the buttons.
commonErrors.prevention: Apply product to the cloth, wipe the surface, keep liquid away from the controls, and dry afterwards.

commonErrors.error: Working on a lift mechanism, door or sensor to fix a fault.
commonErrors.prevention: Report the fault at once. Lift repair and maintenance belong to the lift service company.

commonErrors.error: Leaving a missed visit blank in the record.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the visit as missed, give the reason, and tell the manager.

commonErrors.error: Setting the schedule from memory with no written agreement.
commonErrors.prevention: Agree the schedule in writing with the manager, keep a copy on site, and record each review.

commonErrors.error: Carrying out heavy wet work in peak use without signs or barriers.
commonErrors.prevention: Schedule the work outside peak use, and put up signs and barriers where the area is in use.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Queensland: the WorkSafe Queensland lifts page names installation of a new unit and repair or modernisation of an existing unit as licence categories, and it does not name a licence for servicing or cleaning. The page says the licence type depends on the work (WorkSafe Queensland, lifts and escalators licence page; no date shown). This lesson does not grant any lift licence and does not authorise lift repair, modernisation or mechanism work.

New South Wales: the SafeWork NSW lifts page states that records of inspection and maintenance must be kept, that people with management or control of lifts must make sure they are regularly inspected and maintained, and that a malfunctioning lift must be taken out of service by the service company or building management until repaired. The page does not name a high risk work licence for lift work, and it does not mention cleaning (SafeWork NSW, lifts and escalators page; modified 28 July 2023).

Chemicals used in lift and lobby cleaning must be managed under the label and the SDS. Safe Work Australia states that copies of the SDS must be kept for chemicals used in the hazardous chemical register, and that they must be easily accessible to workers (no date shown).

qualityStandard: The schedule is built with the manager, showing area, frequency, method, products and time window, with high-touch points on their own lines.
The lift is cleaned from the outside with approved methods, and liquid is kept away from the controls in the simulation.
A simulated lift fault is reported at once, with no panel opened and no mechanism touched, and the manager is told in the case study.
Each visit, and each missed visit with its reason, is recorded.
documentationEvidence: Agreed service schedule, with the date, the reviewer and the signed agreement of the manager.
Visit records with the time, the method, the products, defects and the person who did the work.
Fault report for any lift or door fault, with the time, the manager informed and any closure notice.
Record of any missed visit, with the reason and the date the manager was told.
summary: Build the schedule with the manager, put high-touch points on their own lines, and record each review.
Clean lifts from the outside, keep liquid away from the controls, and do not open panels or work on the mechanism.
Report faults at once, and record every visit, including missed visits.

knowledgeChecks.question: A lift button sticks during a clean. What is correct?
options: Open the panel and try to fix it quickly with a small tool
Ignore it, because the lift still moves up and down the building
Report it at once to the manager, and do not work on the mechanism
Spray the button with more product to clear it fast and well

knowledgeChecks.question: How must a missed visit be shown in the visit record?
options: Leave the line blank on the record sheet for the day and the visit
Record it as missed, with the reason and the time the manager was told
Record it as cleaned, because the schedule was met on paper
Remove the line from the record entirely at the end of the day

knowledgeChecks.question: When should heavy wet work be scheduled in a busy lobby?
options: During peak use, because more people will see the work being done
Whenever it is convenient for the cleaner, the crew and the day of the week
Outside peak use, with signs and barriers, and the time agreed with the manager
At the same time as the lift is in use by residents, visitors and the staff
